blocks.title: Newtypes for type safety
blocks.md: Besides the orphan rule, newtypes help in two more ways. They make units and IDs **distinct types**: a function taking `Millimeters` cannot be given `Meters`, and a `UserId(u64)` cannot be passed where an `OrderId(u64)` is expected. And they **hide** an implementation: `People(HashMap<i32, String>)` exposes only the methods you write, so the inner type can change later.

blocks.title: Type aliases
blocks.md: `type Kilometers = i32;` creates an **alias**: another name for the same type. Unlike a newtype, there is no type checking between them; a `Kilometers` and an `i32` mix freely. Aliases are for shortening long types:

blocks.title: The never type
Dynamically sized types and Sized
blocks.md: Rust must know the size of every value at compile time. A few types do not have one: **dynamically sized types** (DSTs), such as `str` (any number of bytes), `[T]` and `dyn Trait`. You can never have a value of these types directly, only behind a pointer that also stores the size: `&str` and `&[T]` hold a length, `&dyn Trait` and `Box<dyn Trait>` hold a vtable (chapter 18).

blocks.title: Function pointers
blocks.md:
A function can be passed where a function is expected, as a value of type **`fn`** (lowercase), the **function pointer** type: `fn(i32) -> i32`. Unlike the closure traits `Fn`, `FnMut`, `FnOnce` (which are traits), `fn` is a concrete type. Function pointers implement all three closure traits, so a function can go anywhere a closure can. The reverse is not true: a closure that captures variables is not an `fn`.

Use `fn` when interfacing with C (which has function pointers but no closures), or when you want a simple concrete type; otherwise prefer generics over `Fn` to accept both.

blocks.title: Returning closures
blocks.md: Every closure has its own unique, unnameable type. To return one, use **`impl Fn(...)`**: "some type implementing this trait". But `impl Trait` stands for **one** concrete type, so two functions returning `impl Fn(i32) -> i32` return **different** types, and they cannot go into the same `Vec`:

   = note: distinct uses of `impl Trait` result in different opaque types

blocks.md: The fix is a trait object, `Box<dyn Fn(i32) -> i32>`: one type for all of them, with dynamic dispatch. A function that must return **different** closures on different branches needs a box for the same reason.

blocks.title: Functions as values
blocks.goal: Accept function pointers, return closures with impl Fn and Box<dyn Fn>, and use ?Sized and the never type.
blocks.behavior:
- `pub fn apply_n(f: fn(i64) -> i64, n: usize, x: i64) -> i64`: apply `f` to `x`, `n` times.
- `pub fn make_adder(k: i64) -> impl Fn(i64) -> i64`.
- `pub fn make_counter() -> impl FnMut() -> u32`: each call returns 1, 2, 3, ...
- `pub fn pipeline(steps: &[&str]) -> Box<dyn Fn(i64) -> i64>`: build one function from step names `"inc"` (+1), `"double"` (*2), `"neg"` (negate), applied left to right; unknown names are skipped; an empty list is the identity.
- `pub fn longest_len<T: AsRef<str> + ?Sized>(items: &[&T]) -> usize`: the length of the longest item, working for `&[&str]` and `&[&String]`.
- `pub fn parse_or_exit(s: &str) -> i64`: parse, or `panic!("bad number: {s}")`. Use a `match` where the error arm has type `!`.
hints: `make_counter` needs `let mut n = 0; move || { n += 1; n }`.
`pipeline`: start with `let mut f: Box<dyn Fn(i64) -> i64> = Box::new(|x| x);` and for each step wrap it: `f = Box::new(move |x| prev(x) * 2)` where `prev` is the old `f` moved into the closure.
blocks.solution_explain: `apply_n` takes an `fn`, so non-capturing closures and functions like `i64::abs` both fit. `pipeline` must return different closure types from one place, so it boxes them; each new box owns the previous one. `?Sized` lets `T` be `str` itself.

questions.q: What is the difference between `type Km = i32;` and `struct Km(i32);`?
options: The alias is the same type as i32; the newtype is a distinct type
The alias is a distinct type

questions.q: Why can `Err(_) => continue` appear in a match whose other arm is a u32?
options: continue has type !, which coerces to any type
It is a special case for loops

questions.q: Which is a dynamically sized type?
questions.explanation: The others are pointers or owned buffers with known size.

questions.q: Can a closure that captures a variable be passed as `fn(i32) -> i32`?
options: No; only non-capturing closures coerce to fn pointers

questions.q: Why can't two functions returning `impl Fn(i32) -> i32` share a Vec?
options: impl Trait is not allowed in Vec
Each stands for a different concrete type

points: Newtypes create distinct types; type aliases only rename.
`!` is the type of diverging expressions and coerces to any type.
DSTs (`str`, `[T]`, `dyn Trait`) live behind pointers; `?Sized` accepts them in generics.
`fn` is a concrete function pointer type and implements all closure traits.
Return closures with `impl Fn` for one type, `Box<dyn Fn>` for several.

terms.def: Another name for an existing type, declared with type Name = Type;.
!, the type of expressions that never produce a value, like panic! or continue.
A type whose size is known only at run time, such as str, [T] or dyn Trait.
A bound that relaxes the default Sized requirement on a generic parameter.
A value of type fn(...) -> ... pointing to a function or non-capturing closure.
